column2: The frontier settlement has brought peace with Britain, but its territorial provisions remain incomplete around Mabhudu. The treaty includes this administration in the republic's new frontier, even where its former relationship with the Zulu kingdom has already lapsed. Our representatives now complete the transfer of its surviving lands and register republican claims over them. Local officials must arrange the passage of public accounts and authority without reopening the campaign or extending the agreement into unrelated neighbouring territory. This implements the settlement already accepted by the raad, rather than a fresh demand upon Britain or the remaining Cape. Mabhudu's separate administration ends as its districts enter the South African Republic.
Complete the agreed incorporation of Mabhudu.
